question.problem:
The function $g(x)$ is defined for every real number $x$ and is given by

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{6}^{2x+a}, & x\ne 0, \\ 36, & x=0.\end{aligned}
$$

If $g(x)$ is continuous at $x=0,$ what is the the value of $a?$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $g(x),$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}{6}^{2x+a}={6}^{a}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}g(x) & =g(0) \\ {6}^{a} & =36 \\ {6}^{a} & ={6}^{2} \\ a & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $a=2$ removes the point discontinuity.
